clues.text: This city in Sweden sits on an inlet of the Baltic Sea. People count it as a true coastal place.
clues.narrowing: rules out everything outside the Baltic coast of Sweden

source.quote: The city is located near the open Baltic Sea on the Stadsfjärden inlet, and is regarded as a coastal location.

clues.text: Warm summers meet winters that hover near freezing point here. Its snow cover comes and goes in the cold months.
clues.narrowing: rules out Baltic coasts with harsh snowy winters or mild frost-free ones; leaves the warm-summer, near-freezing-winter band

source.quote: It retains an oceanic/continental climate hybrid, causing warm summers and winters around the freezing point with variable snow cover.

clues.text: Before twelve thirty, old records used a different name for this town. Then its new name showed up on coins that year.
clues.narrowing: rules out Swedish coastal towns whose current name does not first appear on coins around 1230

source.quote: Nyköping is the name that appears on coins in 1230 and in historical records from the 13th century. Aros is the name of the town found in the archaeological records from before 1230, indicating a new era and a new name sometime around 1230.

clues.text: For thousands of years, the land under downtown was a chain of islands. Its hills were islands, and its flat land was sea floor.
clues.narrowing: rules out Baltic towns whose downtown was not once an island chain with a sea-floor plain

source.quote: For thousands of years, the land of downtown Nyköping was an archipelago where the hills in town today formed many islands, while the flatter parts of the town were the seafloor.

clues.text: This city is home to Stockholm Skavsta Airport. The airport sits just a short trip from the city centre.
clues.narrowing: confirms the Swedish coastal city that hosts Stockholm Skavsta Airport

source.quote: Nyköping is also the home of Stockholm Skavsta Airport, which is located less than 10 kilometres (6.2 mi) from the city centre.
